question.text: Lotus Capital AIF, a SEBI-registered Category II fund structured as a determinate, irrevocable contributory trust, earns INR 40 crore of long-term capital gains on the exit from an unlisted portfolio company during FY 2025-26. Under Section 115UB read with Section 10(23FBA) of the ITA, how is this income taxed?

answer.text: Taxed at the fund level at MMR (39% effective) because AIFs are assessed as AOPs.
Taxed at the fund level at 12.5% LTCG rate and then distributed net of tax to unitholders without any further tax in investor hands.
Taxed at 20% STCG rate at the fund level since the AIF is the direct seller of the shares.
Exempt in the fund's hands; taxed directly in the hands of the unitholders as LTCG on unlisted shares at 12.5% plus applicable surcharge and cess.

explanation.text: The Logic: Category I and II AIFs enjoy pass-through status for all income other than business income. The INR 40 crore LTCG is exempt at the fund level and flows through to unitholders retaining its character as LTCG on unlisted shares. Each unitholder is taxed on their pro-rata share at the unlisted-share LTCG rate of 12.5% plus applicable surcharge and cess. No tax is levied at the fund level on this pass-through income. The Trap: Option A applies a fund-level MMR treatment that does not apply to Cat I/II pass-through income. Option B invents a fund-level capital-gains tax that does not exist under the pass-through regime. Option C misclassifies long-term gain as STCG and ignores the pass-through entirely. Note: The workbook supports Cat I/II pass-through for non-business income, taxation in unitholder hands with the same character, and a 12.5% LTCG rate on unlisted shares plus applicable surcharge and cess.
